I'm stopping before the fix. The fix needs a force-push to `release/2.3`, which rewrites a branch other people have already fetched, and I can't undo that once it's pushed. You asked me to execute the plan, and its Step 5 only covers a normal push. I'll run only read-only checks now.

<command>
git log --oneline -5 release/2.3
</command>
<command>
git show --stat --format='%H %an %s' 7c1d9e0
</command>
<command>
git ls-remote origin release/2.3
</command>
<command>
git rev-list --objects --all | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectname) %(objectsize) %(rest)' | awk '$1=="blob" && $3>52428800'
</command>

The checks confirm four things:
- `7c1d9e0` is still the tip, with no commits on top of it.
- The zip is the only thing in that commit besides the intended `ferry/times.py` and `tests/test_times.py`.
- The remote still points at `7c1d9e0`.
- No other blob over 50 MB sits anywhere in history.

No file edits yet.

**Message to partner:**

Task 4's review found one Important issue. Commit `7c1d9e0` includes `samples/full-season.zip` (310 MB), which the task never asked for, and Step 5 already pushed it to `release/2.3`. The nightly build servers clone that branch, so this breaks your 50 MB rule. A follow-up commit that deletes the file would leave it in history, so the only real fix is to amend `7c1d9e0` and force-push.

I haven't done that yet. Force-pushing `release/2.3` rewrites a shared branch, and two teammates fetched `7c1d9e0` this morning.

Once you approve, I will:
1. Resume the Task 4 implementer to amend `7c1d9e0` without the zip, re-run `uv run pytest -q tests/test_times.py` (expecting `2 passed`), and report the command and output. This counts as fix round 1.
2. Run the scoped re-review on the amended commit.
3. After a clean re-review, run `git push --force-with-lease=release/2.3:7c1d9e0 origin release/2.3`, so the push fails if anyone has pushed since.
4. Mark Task 4 complete in the ledger and continue the plan.

What to expect:
- **Teammates:** the two who fetched it need `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/release/2.3`, or a rebase of any work on top. Their local clones keep the 310 MB object until they gc.
- **Remote:** the old commit may stay reachable on the host (PR refs, caches) until it garbage-collects. If the host keeps it, you may need a host-side purge. Fresh nightly clones normally won't fetch it.

Do you approve the force-push to `release/2.3`? If you'd rather handle the push yourself, I can finish the local amend and re-review and stop before it.
